summary:
MarsWalk Route Planner is an interactive, web-based Martian surface navigation tool built for future human explorers in Jezero Crater (18.44°N, 77.45°E). Using Leaflet.js and real orbital elevation tiles from NASA’s Mars Trek (MGS MOLA/HRSC), we developed a layered map dashboard that integrates terrain topography, a verified 9.2 km low-slope EVA traverse route, geological hazard zones, and high-priority science sample waypoints into a single view.

It directly addresses the Interplanetary Survival Guide challenge by allowing astronauts to toggle hazard zones—such as steep crater rims (>25° slope) and deep sand ripple fields—against safe basalt corridors and Mars 2020 Perseverance science targets like the ancient river delta and Neretva Vallis channel. This unified spatial awareness is critical for keeping crewed Marswalks safe from terrain entrapment while maximizing scientific return during time-limited surface missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

MarsWalk Route Planner is an interactive, web-based Martian surface navigation dashboard centered on Jezero Crater (18.44°N, 77.45°E). Using Leaflet.js configured in planetary Equirectangular projection (EPSG:4326) and live orbital elevation tiles from NASA’s Mars Trek (MGS MOLA + HRSC Color Hillshade), the application overlays three toggleable mission layers onto real Martian terrain:

1. Safe EVA Traverse Route: A verified 9.2 km low-slope (<8°) basalt corridor connecting the Octavia E. Butler Landing habitat hub to the western river delta front and Neretva Vallis inlet.

2. Terrain & Slope Hazards: Interactive hazard polygons marking steep crater rim walls (>25° slope, high rockfall and traction risk) and the Séítah boulder and aeolian sand field (high boot and rover entrapment risk).

3. Science Sample Waypoints: Clickable mission markers detailing priority geological sites for mudstone biosignature and fluvial conglomerate core sampling.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Future human explorers on Mars will operate under strict oxygen and time limits where stepping into deep aeolian sand ripples or steep crater walls can be mission-critical. Instead of cross-referencing disconnected orbital datasets, MarsWalk Route Planner unifies elevation relief, terrain hazards, and high-value science targets into a single browser interface—helping astronauts plan safer routes while maximizing scientific return.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Languages & Libraries: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6), and Leaflet.js (v1.9.4)

- Development & Hosting: Google Antigravity, GitHub, and Vercel (deployed as a static web app)

- Data Sources: NASA Mars Trek WMTS Tile Service (MGS MOLA/HRSC) and NASA Mars 2020 (Perseverance) Jezero Crater geological coordinates

Creativity & Design Factors Considered:

Rather than building a generic 2D map, we aligned the web GIS projection (EPSG:4326) directly with NASA’s planetary tile servers and modeled real operational EVA constraints—specifically slope thresholds (<8° safe traverse vs. >25° hazard zones) and surface traction hazards documented by the Mars 2020 mission.
